answer.text: The portfolio trades 2× its value annually

explanation.text: The Logic: Portfolio turnover ratio is conventionally calculated as the lesser of purchases or sales over a year divided by the portfolio's average AUM. A turnover of 200% therefore implies the portfolio's trading volume in a year is equivalent to twice the portfolio's value — i.e. the manager has effectively replaced the portfolio twice over. The Trap: 'All stocks held for 2 years' confuses turnover with holding period; 'low turnover' contradicts the 200% figure; and 'passive' funds typically run turnover close to zero, not 200%. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook discusses high vs low turnover, frequent trading, transaction costs and rebalancing costs (around pp. 219, 306, 319, 396) but does not define the turnover ratio formula or this specific 200% interpretation. The framing above is general industry/regulatory knowledge.
